name: terminal-buttons
description: Small status bar buttons for running files, stopping terminal work, and changing directories.

commands.title: Terminal Buttons: Set Active Terminal Path Mode

terminalButtons.preferActiveTerminal.description: Use the active terminal when one exists. When disabled, commands use a dedicated Terminal Buttons terminal.

terminalButtons.enableDefaultRunCommands.description: Enable built-in single-file run commands. Disable this when you want terminalButtons.runCommands to be the only source of run behavior.

terminalButtons.autoDetectRuntimes.description: Detect relevant runtime commands lazily and cache the result. Project-local TypeScript runners are checked before PATH commands.

terminalButtons.stopBehavior.description: How the Stop button stops terminal work. Restart recreates the terminal process; interrupt sends Ctrl+C; dispose closes the terminal.

terminalButtons.statusBarPriority.description: Status bar priority for the CD button. Run and Stop are placed immediately to its left. Lower values move right-aligned items farther right.

run.description: Status bar foreground color for Run.

stop.description: Status bar foreground color for Stop.

cd.description: Status bar foreground color for CD.

terminalButtons.colors.description: Status bar foreground colors for the terminal buttons. Use CSS colors such as #00FF66.

terminalButtons.pathStyle.description: How file paths are formatted before sending commands. Auto detects WSL-like Windows terminals.

terminalButtons.terminalName.description: Name for the dedicated terminal when terminalButtons.preferActiveTerminal is disabled or no terminal is active.

terminalButtons.tools.description: Override tool commands or executable paths used by built-in defaults. Keys include node, tsx, ts-node, bun, deno, python, python3, py, go, java, php, ruby, bash, sh, pwsh, and more.

terminalButtons.runCommands.description: Custom run commands keyed by basename, extension, *.extension, extension without the dot, language id, folder, or default. Templates support ${file}, ${fileRaw}, ${fileDirname}, ${folder}, ${workspaceFolder}, ${relativeFile}, ${fileBasename}, ${fileBasenameNoExtension}, and raw variants.

scripts.test: npm run compile && npm run lint && node --test out/test/*.test.js
